chapter_title: Checking and Calibrating AI Agent Output
learning_objective: The learner will calculate the range and the median of five runs for each of six metrics and decide whether each metric is stable or unstable, with at least 5 of 6 metrics fully correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** run-variance-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** calculate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will calculate the range and the median of five runs for each of six metrics and decide whether each metric is stable or unstable, with at least 5 of 6 metrics fully correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Run-to-Run Variance, Agent Disagreement (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each metric the learner enters the range, enters the median, and chooses Stable or Unstable. A metric is fully correct when all three match the Content table. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 metrics fully correct on the first attempt. Viewing the rule is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) An average that matches the humans means the agent is reliable. (2) One run is enough. (3) The median is the same as the average. **Instructional Rationale:** Computing a range and a median is an Apply-level action. Metrics that include a stable one, a one-run outlier, and a wide spread teach the learner to look at the spread and not only the center. **Content:** The rule, shown at all times: the range is the highest run minus the lowest run. A metric is Stable when its range is <= 1 and Unstable when its range is >= 2. An unstable metric goes to a human reviewer. The six metrics (all for the made-up resource Watershed Basics): | # | Metric | Five runs | Range | Median | Verdict | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Accuracy and currency | 7, 7, 7, 7, 7 | 0 | 7 | Stable | All five runs agree. | | 2 | Alignment | 6, 6, 5, 6, 6 | 1 | 6 | Stable | One run is a point lower, and the range is 1. | | 3 | Readability | 8, 8, 8, 9, 8 | 1 | 8 | Stable | One run is a point higher, and the range is 1. | | 4 | Accessibility | 5, 6, 5, 7, 5 | 2 | 5 | Unstable | The range is 2, so a person decides. | | 5 | Practice with feedback | 4, 7, 6, 5, 8 | 4 | 6 | Unstable | The runs spread across five values. | | 6 | Metadata | 4, 4, 4, 4, 4 | 0 | 4 | Stable | All five runs agree. | **Provenance:** The runs are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The stability rule is a teaching choice, and the sim labels it "illustrative threshold". **Rules:** The median is the third value after the five runs are sorted. The range and median are whole numbers. A metric is fully correct only when the range, the median, and the verdict all match. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one metric with its five runs and the rule. 2. The learner enters the range and the median, and chooses Stable or Unstable. 3. The learner presses Check, and the sim shows which of the three answers are correct and the Why text. 4. After metric 6 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 metrics in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: range [range], median [median], [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. The range is [range], the median is [median], and the metric is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can tell a stable metric from an unstable one." Below 5 it lists the Why text of each missed metric. **Starting State:** Metric 1 or the first metric in the shuffled order, with the rule and empty fields. **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's table of five runs on six metrics is the data of this sim. The chapter says an unstable metric goes to a person even if the median matches the human score.
